text:
leah-sales: AcmeCare wants a short POC: Redwood Private in their account, must pass egress through their TLSinspect proxy, and compliance requires original client IPs in request telemetry. They also want a tiny allowlist to put in their firewall change ticket. Thoughts?

toni-neteng: doable but few topology choices + tradeoffs. Quick flavors:
1) PrivateLink (interface endpoint) -> Redwood-managed connector: minimal infra for customer. Downside: endpoint ENI IPs are per-AZ and can change on recreate, so not great for a strict static allowlist. Also PrivateLink terminates TLS at the endpoint so X-Forwarded-For must be injected by customer's proxy.
2) Deploy connector (NLB + backend ASG) in customer VPC: gives stable EIPs (NLB preservation) and connector sees original client IP when using NLB with proxy protocol or TCP passthrough. This is my recommended POC for audits.

oliver-se: To add: ALB (HTTPS) will terminate TLS and you lose source IP unless you use X-Forwarded-For header. NLB (TCP) preserves client IP at TCP layer and works better with TLS-inspect bypasses / passthrough. If customer's proxy inspects TLS and rewrites source, only the proxy IP will be visible unless the proxy forwards X-Forwarded-For.

mia-ps: They asked whether we can support mutual TLS between their clients and the connector, and whether KMS is supported for keys.

toni-neteng: mTLS: yes, connector supports client cert validation at termination. If using NLB TCP passthrough, mutual TLS must be handled by the connector (i.e., terminate TLS on connector), or you can terminate at proxy and use mutual auth between app and proxy. KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption; we'll provide a KMS key ARN you can point to in config.

leah-sales: Ok for the firewall ticket we need a 3-line pasteable entry they can submit right away (they have a weekly change window). Can we get two variants (NLB EIP option and PrivateLink option)?

toni-neteng: Paste these. Variant A (connector-in-VPC, preferred for stable IPs):
```
# Firewall ticket - Variant A (Connector deployed in-customer VPC)
Allow TCP/443 from App Subnet 10.20.0.0/22 to Connector NLB EIPs 198.51.100.21 and 198.51.100.22 (outbound)
Allow TCP/443 from Connector NLB EIPs to App ALB / ELB security group (inbound) if using callback flows
```
Variant B (PrivateLink/interface endpoint):
```
# Firewall ticket - Variant B (AWS Interface Endpoint)
Allow TCP/443 from App Subnet 10.20.0.0/22 to Interface Endpoint ENI IPs (to be provided after endpoint creation). Note: ENI IPs are per-AZ and may change; request follow-up to update allowlist if endpoint is recreated.
```
Also include note: if customer's TLS proxy SNATs traffic, request X-Forwarded-For preservation from proxy team.

oliver-se: Sample security group/iptables examples for connector hosts:
```
# sg: connector-sg
Inbound: TCP 443 from 10.20.0.0/22
Inbound: TCP 22 from 10.20.1.0/24 (ops only)
Outbound: TCP 443 to 0.0.0.0/0 (model fetches)
# iptables (optional)
-A INPUT -p tcp --dport 9100 -s 10.20.0.0/22 -j ACCEPT  # metrics (if exposed)
```

mia-ps: Pricing/context note for procurement: PrivateLink = customer pays AWS endpoint hourly + data processing (per-GB). Connector-in-VPC = customer pays EC2/NLB/EIP costs; Redwood applies Private deployment POC credit for first 30 days. I'll add a short line in the quote.

infra-bot: Provisioned ephemeral connector stack in acct 210987654321 (us-west-2). stack-id: poc-connector-789. NLB fronted, ALB disabled.

leah-sales: Great. Two operational questions: 1) can we provide stable request IDs so AcmeCare can correlate logs with their SIEM? 2) can we forward logs to their Syslog/TLS endpoint?

toni-neteng: 1) yes — connector emits a UUID request_id per request and includes X-Request-Id in responses (if present). 2) we support push to customer syslog over TLS and/or S3. For POC, simplest is S3 log export with short retention; for production we can enable persistent TLS syslog forwarder.

oliver-se: Also note: if they require preservation of original client IP at application layer and their proxy is doing TLS inspect, recommend configuring the proxy to add X-Forwarded-For and avoid SNAT, or place NLB in front of connector and allow the proxy to pass-through traffic (no TLS inspect) for those flows. We'll document the exact proxy policy snippet they need.

leah-sales: Owners and next actions:
- toni-neteng: produce final two-line firewall ticket + 1-page network runbook (due tomorrow EOD)
- mia-ps: add POC credit note to quote and confirm expected infra cost ballpark (due EOD)
- oliver-se: fill security questionnaire lines for mTLS/KMS/log forwarding and send to AcmeCare (due EOD)
- leah-sales: schedule 30m handoff during change window (I'll coordinate)

leah-sales: If anyone can drop a one-liner summarizing IP preservation tradeoff I can paste into the SOC ticket, do it here.

toni-neteng: One-liner: "To preserve original client IPs use an NLB TCP passthrough or ensure your TLS proxy forwards X-Forwarded-For and does not SNAT; PrivateLink is easier to run but ENI IPs are ephemeral."

oliver-se: I'll attach a short diagram + proxy config snippet in the runbook.
